cards.question:
Determine ΔH from this reaction pathway diagram. Then sketch the same profile and label the forward activation-energy interval as additional practice. [1]

Diagram description: vertical axis relative enthalpy / kJ mol⁻¹; horizontal axis reaction progress. The reactant level is 0, the peak is +80, and the product level is −40.
cards.answer: ΔH = −40 kJ mol⁻¹ [1], because products lie 40 kJ mol⁻¹ below reactants. In the practice sketch, label enthalpy and progress axes, reactants and products, and the activation interval from reactants to the peak (80 kJ mol⁻¹).

cards.question:
Determine the functional group supported by the labelled strong band in this synthetic IR spectrum. Supplied reference: strong C=O absorption 1670–1750 cm⁻¹. [1]

Diagram description: a synthetic percentage-transmittance spectrum, with wavenumber decreasing from 4000 to 500 cm⁻¹. A strong absorption minimum is labelled 1720 cm⁻¹. Other illustrative C–H and fingerprint-region absorptions are shown. The trace does not identify a unique compound.
cards.answer: A carbonyl C=O group [1], supported by the labelled 1720 cm⁻¹ absorption. This alone does not uniquely identify the molecule.
cards.lesson_title: (L1)Shapes of organic molecules AND Infra-red spectroscopy

cards.question:
Describe the actions and observation points shown in this diagram.

Diagram description: three boxes linked by arrows. The first says fresh portion of sample X. The second says add reagent dropwise and record the initial effect. The third says add excess of the same reagent and record the final effect.
cards.answer: Take a fresh portion of X; follow the diagram arrow to add reagent dropwise and record the initial effect; then add excess of the same reagent and record whether the precipitate remains or dissolves.

cards.question:
Determine the rate trend shown by the gas-volume graph over0–40 s and40–80 s, using supporting volumes.

Diagram description: gas volume / cm³ on the vertical axis, time / s on the horizontal axis. The horizontal scale runs from 0 to 100 s and the vertical scale from 0 to 65 cm³. The model curve passes through approximately (0 s, 0 cm³), (40 s, 37.9 cm³), and (80 s, 51.9 cm³). A red tangent is drawn at 40 s.
cards.answer: The graph rises from0 to about37.9 cm³ by40 s and then to about51.9 cm³ by80 s. Smaller gain in the second equal interval supports a declining average rate.

cards.question:
Determine the unknown concentration by reading the calibration graph at its indicated signal0.70.

Diagram description: dimensionless signal on the vertical axis, concentration / mol dm⁻³ on the horizontal axis. The concentration scale runs from 0.01 to 0.05 mol dm⁻³ and the signal scale from 0.0 to 1.2. Measured standards and a straight fitted line are shown. A horizontal guide marks the unknown signal 0.70.
cards.answer: The horizontal signal0.70 guide meets the fitted line at concentration about0.030 mol dm−3. Read the corresponding x-coordinate; this is interpolation within the measured range.
